title: SURFACING SEMANTIC ORTHOGONALITY ACROSS MODEL SAFETY BENCHMARKS: A MULTI-DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS

bias_targets.methodology: Using embedding models, UMAP dimensionality reduction, and k-means clustering on prompt strings to identify semantic coverage gaps, redundancies, and asymmetric representation of harm categories (e.g., self-harm vs. privacy) across different AI safety benchmarks.

Comparing prompt length distributions and density across five AI safety benchmarks using kernel density estimation and outlier removal to reveal structural confounds and differing assessment approaches (short vulnerability prompts vs. nuanced real-world scenarios).
